{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United Kingdom|Cuisine of the UK]]

Any good pastry dough can be used for Cornish pasties, but it should be neither too rich nor too flaky. This works very well. Adjust amounts as required.

See also [[Cookbook:Pasties]].

==Ingredients==

* 1 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] (450 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]
* ½ lb (225 g) mixture of [[Cookbook:Lard|lard]], [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], and/or [[Cookbook:Suet|suet]] (equal ratios)
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* Water
== Procedure ==
#Combine the dry ingredients, then gradually mix in enough water to make a stiff [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]].
#[[Cookbook:Dough#Rolling|Roll]] dough to about a ¼ inch thick.
#Cut out rounds with a tea plate—or other round object about 6in across.
#Lay rounds on a pastry-board with half the round propped on a [[Cookbook:Rolling Pin|rolling-pin]]. Add the filling, and fold dough over filling.
#Dampen the edges with water, and press to seal. Crimp the edges, then make slit in middle of each pasty.
#Place on [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|baking sheet]], [[Cookbook:Bake|bake]] in hot oven (450 °F) until golden-brown.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Try using vegetarian equivalents for the fats.
* Omit salt for low-sodium diet, or use low-sodium salt.

== References ==
* ''from'' Cornish Recipes, Ancient & Modern, 22nd Edition, The Cornwall Federation of Women's Institutes 1965. ''First collected & published by'' Edith Martin, Tregavethan, Truro, 1929, ''for'' The Cornwall F.of W. I.
